messages.author: 09fd833635384d0f
messages.subject: INLA crash message
parts:
Hi everyone -- I was wondering if someone might be able to help me sort through this error message that I received while running the INLA model. I've attached an error text that I received, and will put the code below that I ran. A helpful note is that the "dataforfit" variable we are using is of size 4255, and the "datapred" variable we are using is of size 4255. We've ran the following code in other geographic areas with sometimes larger numbers of houses for dataforfit and datapred, but for some reason are receiving an error with one such model run. Any help would be really appreciated!:



# create datasets of observations 
dataforfit <- df[which(df$outcome == 1 | df$outcome == 0),]
datapred <- df[which(df$insptime == 4),]

# print out number of observations of each timestep
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 1: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 1))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 2: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 2))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 3: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 3))))
print(paste0("Number of observations from time step 4: ", length(which(dataforfit$insptime == 4))))

# print out sizes of dataforfit and datapred
print(paste0("Size of dataforfit: ", nrow(dataforfit)))
print(paste0("Size of datapred: ", nrow(datapred)))

# define time dimension
k <- length(unique(df$insptime))

# define two coordinate matrices
coords1<- cbind(dataforfit$LONGITUDEscale, dataforfit$LATITUDEscale)
coords <- cbind(datapred$LONGITUDEscale, datapred$LATITUDEscale)

# create mesh
mesh1 <- inla.mesh.2d(coords1, max.edge=c(50*S,50*S), cutoff=0.2)

# create two A matrices
A.est <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh1,
                          loc=coords1,
                          group=dataforfit$insptime,n.group=k)

A.prd <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh1, loc=coords, group=datapred$insptime)

# create SPDE object of Matern covariance matrix
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh1, 
                          alpha=2,
                          theta.prior.mean=c(8,-5),
                          theta.prior.prec=c(50,50))

# create mesh index
mesh.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name='spatial', 
                                   n.spde=spde$n.spde,n.group=k)

# create stack object for data for fit
stack.est =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=dataforfit$outcome),
             A=list(A.est,1),
             effects=
               list(c(mesh.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(
                      not_sprayed=dataforfit$not_sprayed)),
             tag="est")

# create stack object for data for prediction
stack.pred =
  inla.stack(data=list(y=datapred$outcome),
             A=list(A.prd,1),
             effects=
               list(c(mesh.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                    list(
                      not_sprayed=datapred$not_sprayed)),
             tag="pred")

# combine stack objects  
stack = inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred)

# formula to input into INLA
formula <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + not_sprayed + f(spatial, 
                                                model=spde, 
                                                group=spatial.group, 
                                                control.group=list(model='ar1', 
                                                                   hyper=list(theta=list(prior='pccor1', param=c(0, 0.9)))))

#===================================================================================
# IVc. Run INLA model
#===================================================================================

# priors are set by control.fixed
result <- inla(formula,
               data = inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
               family = c("binomial"),verbose=TRUE,
               #control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE,link=1)  # Produces estimates
               control.predictor = list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE,link=1)
               ,control.inla = list(reordering = "metis")
               ,control.fixed = list(mean = list(Intercept=-6.9, not_sprayed=1.97), # Prior means,obtain form Corentin model
                                     prec = list(Intercept=50, not_sprayed=50))  #inverse of the variance 
               #,num.threads=4  # uses 4 cores may be helpful
)

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crash message
parts:
Hi,

I cannot guess the error based on the error output, unfortunately. Can you try out
- num.threads=1
- having a different prediction and estimation length
- remove the intercept from the stack and the formula
- Making sure you have enough memory in your computer

If you try one of them at a time, that could tell us why it crashes.

By the way, what is your mesh$n and k?

Best,
Haakon

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA crash message
parts:
What's the size of the model (4 timesteps it seems, but what is
spde$n.spde?) The size of the data is not very important, since for
these models it's usually much smaller than the model itself.

What's the output of
str(stack)
?

Finn
